questions.q: Where does Oracle publish its REST API documentation for Financials?
options: Only inside the Oracle Fusion application itself, with no public page
docs.oracle.com, in a guide organized by resource
A random community wiki with no official status
It is not documented anywhere
questions.explain: Oracle publishes an official REST API guide for Financials on docs.oracle.com.

questions.q: What does the request body schema on a documentation page tell you?
options: The visual theme of the Oracle Fusion UI
Which fields a POST or PATCH operation accepts, and which are required
The server's IP address
How many users are logged in
questions.explain: The request body schema lists every field the operation accepts and flags which are required.

questions.q: Why does the documentation URL include a Fusion release, like 25D or 26A?
options: It's just decorative text with no meaning
Because resources and fields can change slightly between Fusion releases
Because it indicates the user's time zone
Because it is the invoice date format
questions.explain: The release version matters because resource shapes can evolve between Fusion releases.

questions.q: What is the most common avoidable cause of a 400 error when creating a record via REST?
options: Sending a required field that's missing or malformed, because the documentation wasn't checked first
The Oracle Fusion server being down
Using the GET method instead of POST
Using JSON instead of XML
questions.explain: Skipping the documented required-fields check is the most common avoidable cause of a 400.

questions.q: On a documentation page for a GET operation, where would you find out that 'limit' and 'offset' are supported?
options: The response schema section
The request parameters section
The page's title only
They are never documented and must be guessed
questions.explain: Supported query parameters like limit, offset, q, fields, and expand are listed in the request parameters section.
